observation.title: Stores — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. The shape of the object you pass is the API of the store. import { forge } from "runeforge"; const session = forge({ state: { user: null as User | null, expiresAt: 0 }, actions: { login: (s, user: User, ttl: number) => ({ user, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl }), logout: () => ({ user: null, expiresAt: 0 }), }, }); The returned store is a plain object with these methods, plus your actions as methods: MEMBER SIGNATURE DESCRIPTION get () => State Returns the current state (a frozen snapshot). set (next: Partial<State>) => void Imperative state update. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. Reading and subscribing The simplest store is read with get() and observed with subscribe(): const current = session.get(); // { user: null, expiresAt: 0 } const off = session.subscribe((next, prev) => { console.log("changed:", prev, "→", next); }); // later off(); State is immutable. Each commit replaces the previous state with a new frozen object. Don't try to mutate s.user.name = "x" — return a new object instead. Runeforge will warn in dev if it detects an in-place mutation. Composing stores Apps usually have several stores. They compose by importing each other and using derive(): import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { session } from "./session"; import { feed } from "./feed"; export const homepage = derive( [session, feed], (s, f) => ({ greeting: s.user ? `Welcome back, ${s.user.name}` : "Welcome", items: s.user ? f.items : f.items.slice(0, 5), }) ); derive only recomputes when one of its inputs changes — and only emits a notification when its output changes (by structural equality). It's the right tool for "computed views" or "memoized selectors". Slicing a store For very large stores, store.select() returns a slice that behaves like its own store: const currentUser = session.select((s) => s.user); currentUser.subscribe((u) => render(u)); // fires only when `s.user` changes — not on `expiresAt` changes Server-side rendering & serialization Every store can be serialized with store.toJSON() and rehydrated with store.fromJSON(). The intended flow on the server is: create stores, prime them with fetched data, render once, ship the dehydrated state along with the HTML. // server session.login(user, 3600_000); const html = renderToString(<App />); const state = { session: session.toJSON(), feed: feed.toJSON() }; // client session.fromJSON(state.session); feed.fromJSON(state.feed); hydrate(<App />); Testing stores Stores are easy to unit-test because they have no framework. Just call actions and assert against store.get(): import { session } from "./session"; beforeEach(() => session.reset()); test("login sets the user and expiry", () => { session.login({ id: 1, name: "Milena" }, 60_000); const s = session.get(); expect(s.user?.name).toBe("Milena"); expect(s.expiresAt).toBeGreaterThan(Date.now()); }); PREVIOUS ← Quickstart NEXT Actions & selectors →

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react) HOOK useStore(store, selector?,

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react) HOOK useStore(store, selector?,

ux_notes: Pressing Enter on mobile search changed the URL from examples.html to api-reference.html#forge, so result selection navigated to the intended destination.
The search overlay appears to close cleanly after selection: the destination page content is visible with no search results or modal content obscuring the page, despite DOM still reporting 1 dialog.

Orientation is mixed after navigation: the page title/breadcrumbs in visible text ('Docs › API reference', 'Reference · v3.4', 'API reference.') help confirm location, but the screenshot lands directly in the forge() section rather than showing the anchor heading, reducing immediate confidence that '#forge' was reached.

Mobile clarity is further weakened by layout issues on the destination page, including horizontal overflow (541px page width on 390px viewport) and a partially clipped parameters table/code area in the screenshot.

step.objective: Learn whether changing docs versions on mobile causes a clear, trustworthy state change or repeats the earlier mismatch where the selector changes but page content/version cues do not.
step.success_criteria: The selected version should visibly update and the page content, URL, or version cues should change coherently enough that users can trust which docs version they are viewing.

result.feedback: Selected option 'v3.3'. No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

ux_notes: Changing the mobile version selector to 'v3.3' did not produce a coherent state change: the URL stayed `api-reference.html#forge`, visible branding and breadcrumb still say `Runeforge v3.4` / `Reference · v3.4`, and the tool reported 'No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.'
The version dropdown itself lacks an accessible label in the DOM (`missing_input_label` warning on `ux-3`), which makes version context harder to verify on mobile.

Mobile trust is further weakened by layout issues visible after the selection: the page still has horizontal overflow (`scroll_width 541` on a 390px viewport), so the version control sits in a cramped header while content overflows sideways.

step.objective: Assess whether the overflowing API reference table/code content remains readable and navigable on mobile, or if users must pan/hunt due to clipped columns.
step.success_criteria: The next viewport should expose more of the parameters table/overflowing content, revealing whether columns remain clipped, require horizontal panning, or lose context on mobile.

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux.
